description: Canonical machine-readable topology for runtime systems and agent context tooling (phase-3 route-composer split plus Phase VIII replenishment producer+notification-consumer closure, additive telemetry journaling from websocket ingress through Kafka into Spanner audit storage, retailer cart sync realtime convergence via CART_SYNC_UPDATED post-commit invalidation, retailer AI confirm/reject outbox atomicity plus ORDER_REASSIGNED retailer+supplier fanout parity with admin-portal hybrid invalidation, retailer inbox settlement/session refresh parity with shared ws-event contract coverage, checkout supplier-effective currency resolution, payment-session currency normalization, refund/chargeback additive currency compatibility, treasury/reconciliation read-model currency parity for admin portal consumers, warehouse treasury invoice currency parity across portal and native clients, multitenant driver/factory login disambiguation plus supplier-scoped phone uniqueness in provisioning flows, phase-1 regional substrate plus provider-seam normalization for GLOBAL_PAY/ADYEN/CASH with official Adyen Payment Links hosted-checkout wiring, provider execution-path gateway normalization, supplier/warehouse region query-scope middleware enforcement, webhook route composition parity for Global Pay, Stripe, and Adyen ingress, settlement-locality bootstrap for MasterInvoices/Warehouses/Vault precedence plus SupplierInventoryV2 warehouse-key inventory schema, supplier inventory import staging substrate and admin-portal wizard shell routing, active InventoryV2 runtime dual-read/write mirroring across checkout/restock plus replenishment and planning read convergence, autonomous nearest-factory routing fallback when no active SupplyLanes candidate exists, checkout warehouse equal-H3 tie round-robin balancing across resolver paths, region-filtered supplier reads and expanded warehouse ops plus demand read surfaces, slog observability tranche across high-noise runtime domains and cache infrastructure paths, local sequential-thinking MCP fallback, targeted workspace retrieval as the default codebase-retrieval path, S-level dynamic billing metering with milestone-driven platform fee adjustments plus treasury billing telemetry, and dynamic delivery handshake settlement orchestration with DeliverySessions audit trails, settlement-required fanout, dispute escalation outbox/dispatcher closure, and retailer role-row consumption parity).

methods: Kafka Event ORDER_FINALIZED (TopicMain consumer group pegasus-billing-tier-worker-group)
Spanner RWTxn upsert BillingMeterEvents by OrderId
Spanner RWTxn sharded increments on BillingSupplierMeters and BillingGlobalMeters
SystemConfig updates for platform_fee_basis_points and billing_* milestone keys
notes: Metering is idempotent by OrderId to make ORDER_FINALIZED replay-safe under at-least-once Kafka delivery.
Counter rows are sharded to avoid Spanner write hotspots at scale.
Fee adjustments are milestone-driven and applied through SystemConfig basis points with additive compatibility fallback to percent-based keys.
Order split and ledger math now resolve runtime basis points to keep checkout and treasury views aligned with dynamic fee changes.
Spanner schema now includes InventoryImportSessions and interleaved InventoryImportRows with supplier and warehouse filter indexes for staging and review flows.

Phase-2 compatibility substrate also includes SupplierImportSessions, interleaved SupplierImportStagedRows, and SupplierImportMapping keyed by supplier_id/session_id for strict supplier data isolation.

Phase-3 signed-upload bridge now issues deterministic GCS PUT tickets (imports/{supplier_id}/{session_id}/raw.xlsx), writes SupplierImportSessions in INITIALIZED status pre-ingress, enforces a 50MB upload-size gate, and exposes POST /v1/supplier/inventory/imports/{id}/uploaded to transition UPLOADED + emit outbox INVENTORY_IMPORT_UPLOADED on inventory.import.events.

Phase-4 AI mapping worker now consumes inventory.import.events in apps/ai-worker/import_worker.go, claims sessions into DISCOVERING, streams first-50-row samples from GCS, runs provider-agnostic mapping through packages/ai-bridge (InventoryMapper with Vertex Gemini token counting + deterministic/fallback header logic), persists DISCOVERED or MAPPING_REQUIRED with anomaly summaries into SupplierImportSessions/SupplierImportMapping, and emits INVENTORY_IMPORT_STATUS_UPDATE for supplier websocket IMPORT_STATUS fanout.
Session mapping, approve, and apply handlers now persist staged-row lifecycle state and counters instead of returning not-implemented stubs.
Suppliercoreroutes import sandbox stubs expose /v1/supplier/inventory/imports for session init/status/mapping/approve and enforce supplier_id from JWT scope only.
Staged import inventory audit writes now use BULK_IMPORT_STAGED reason in InventoryAuditLog.

Admin portal now exposes a supplier bulk-import ingress shell at /supplier/inventory/import with upload-ticket, session, rows, mapping, approve, apply, status, direct signed-URL upload, uploaded bridge signal, and processing scanner/skeleton states.

methods: internal PaymentSession settle -> DeliverySessions FINAL_SETTLEMENT update
internal cash collection completion -> DeliverySessions FINAL_SETTLEMENT update
consumers: pegasus/apps/retailer-app-desktop payment and settlement modal flows
pegasus/apps/retailer-app-android payment and settlement modal flows
pegasus/apps/retailer-app-ios payment and settlement modal flows
notes: DeliverySessions and DeliverySessionAdjustments are additive schema surfaces keyed by SessionId with order/driver/retailer/supplier indexes for realtime and audit queries.
VerifyHandshake supports signed JWT tokens with fallback to the existing delivery token path for compatibility while enforcing geofence and assignment checks.

ConfirmOffload now transitions session state to SETTLEMENT_AWAIT and emits SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED; orderroutes websocket fanout emits additive SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED plus legacy PAYMENT_REQUIRED for deployed clients.

Kafka notification dispatcher now consumes DELIVERY_SESSION_UPDATED and projects settlement/session numeric fields onto websocket frames so retailer modal consumers receive amount/session parity during fanout delivery.

Treasury invoice status override now emits DELIVERY_DISPUTED via transactional outbox on DISPUTED transitions, and notification dispatcher consumes DELIVERY_DISPUTED for supplier manual-review fanout.

Retailer desktop, iOS, and Android clients now consume SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED directly and treat DELIVERY_SESSION_UPDATED as additive amount or refresh signal to keep payment and order views converged during settlement.
Active fulfillment query now includes AWAITING_PAYMENT with legacy AWAITING_GLOBAL_PAYNT compatibility to prevent payment-waiting rows from dropping from retailer fulfillment surfaces.
CompleteOrder now blocks completion while delivery-session settlement is still pending (uncleared PaymentClearedAt on active session states).
Payment session settlement and cash collection completion now advance matching delivery sessions to FINAL_SETTLEMENT and record PaymentClearedAt to release delivery lock semantics.
GET returns an additive superset order-detail payload with line items.
GET /v1/orders/{id}/events returns the scoped OrderEvents audit timeline for the same compatibility surface.
PATCH accepts both /status and /state path aliases.
PATCH accepts either status or state in the request body for legacy compatibility.
Unified checkout emits ORDER_VALIDATION_FAILED, PAYMENT_CLEARED, and ORDER_FINALIZED to kafka.TopicMain through transactional outbox, replacing the stale topic.orders.v1 path.

Unified checkout now resolves supplier-effective currency through countrycfg.Service and applies that currency to MasterInvoices, Orders, OrderLineItems, and checkout outbox payloads, with a temporary 422 guard when one checkout payload spans mixed supplier currencies.
MasterInvoices writes now persist additive SettlementTarget values (GLOBAL_SUPPLIER, LOCAL_WAREHOUSE, MIXED_WAREHOUSE) across unified/card/cash checkout flows.
Unified checkout now mirrors effective stock decrements into SupplierInventoryV2 for warehouse-assigned plans while preserving SupplierInventory locks for backward-compatible contention control.
payment/session.go now honors CreateSessionRequest.Currency and preserves the prior session currency during RetryPaymentSession gateway switches.
payment/provider.go now centralizes gateway resolution for GLOBAL_PAY, ADYEN, and CASH; ADYEN resolves to payment/adyen.go (official adyen-go-api-library/v21 Payment Links hosted checkout adapter).

payment/session.go create/attempt/bind/retry paths now normalize gateway values through NewProviderClient, checkout URL generators fail closed for unsupported/unavailable providers, and payment/webhooks.go validates session gateway compatibility through the provider resolver before Global Pay settlement.

order/service.go now initializes Adyen hosted checkout links and binds provider references via SessionService.BindProviderCheckout; direct Adyen charge/refund paths remain explicitly unsupported via ErrAdyenDirectOperationUnsupported.

Refund and chargeback compatibility paths now accept additive amount+currency input while preserving amount_uzs contracts; refund responses include additive amount+currency fields, and anomaly currency writes now resolve from runtime/session currency rather than hardcoded UZS.
webhookroutes now mounts all gateway webhook ingress paths behind shared priority and logging middleware wrappers.

Adyen webhook processing in payment/adyen_webhook.go parses official notification envelopes, validates per-item HMAC signatures, and applies idempotency guards before settlement/failure mutation paths.
Gateway webhook handlers remain signature-first and role-unauthenticated by design.
Read queries now join Retailers and apply auth.AppendRegionFilter on the retailer alias when region scope is active.
Route composers continue to validate region_id compatibility via auth.RequireRegionScopeWithClient before handler execution.
Warehouse ops reads and demand-forecast order-side reads now join Retailers and apply auth.AppendRegionFilter on the retailer alias when region scope is active.
Route composers continue to validate region_id compatibility via auth.RequireRegionScopeWithClient before handler execution.
When no active SupplyLanes row exists for supplier plus warehouse, the optimizer now falls back to nearest active supplier factory instead of returning no candidate.
Fallback applies additive ProductTypes preference when explicit product mappings are present, and then relaxes to all active factories if no explicit mapping matches the requested product.
When warehouse coordinates are unavailable, fallback uses warehouse PrimaryFactoryId or SecondaryFactoryId before deterministic first-candidate selection.
Warehouse candidates are now ranked by H3 grid distance, with equal-ring candidates tie-broken using Redis-backed round-robin counters keyed by wh:rr:<supplierId>:<retailerCell>.
Tie-break distribution applies to both Redis grid-cell and Spanner fallback resolver paths.
When Redis is unavailable or round-robin state cannot advance, selection falls back to deterministic lexical warehouse ordering.

consumers: future supplier telemetry audit read models
notes: WebSocket ingress/egress remains additive JSON for current clients.
Hub derives a deterministic trace_id when the driver payload does not provide one yet.
Kafka journaling is best-effort and non-blocking at ingress; the sink persists replay-safe rows keyed by TraceId.

consumers: pegasus/apps/retailer-app-ios RetailerService order fulfillment tracking and settings flows
pegasus/apps/retailer-app-android RetailerApi order fulfillment tracking and settings flows
notes: Retailer role-row composition now includes idempotency-guarded legacy procurement create and cancel mutations while shared order list/detail/refund compatibility reads live in orderroutes.
This extracted surface centralizes the shared retailer read, payment, settings, and realtime contract across desktop, iOS, and Android.
Retailer desktop and iOS order-list consumers now converge on GET /v1/retailers/{retailerID}/orders, and payment websocket clients handle both canonical PAYMENT_* and legacy GLOBAL_PAYNT_* aliases.
POST /v1/retailer/cart/sync now emits CART_SYNC_UPDATED over ws/retailer post-commit, and desktop, iOS, and Android cart stores rehydrate from GET /v1/retailer/cart/sync when that signal arrives.

POST /v1/retailer/orders/{confirm-ai,reject-ai} now emits AI_ORDER_CONFIRMED/AI_ORDER_REJECTED through transactional outbox in the same Orders mutation transaction, and ORDER_REASSIGNED fanout now includes affected retailer recipients so desktop/iOS/Android order and tracking views refresh on reassignment.

Retailer desktop inbox refresh now includes SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED and DELIVERY_SESSION_UPDATED, iOS/Android inbox icon mappings include ORDER_REASSIGNED plus settlement/session-update event types, and packages/types/ws-events.ts now carries additive retailer ws-event contracts for ORDER_REASSIGNED, SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_SESSION_UPDATED, and CART_SYNC_UPDATED.

Retailer Android push fallback mapping now includes SETTLEMENT_REQUIRED and DELIVERY_SESSION_UPDATED in PegasusFirebaseMessagingService so settlement/session-update alerts remain visible while backgrounded or when websocket delivery is unavailable.
driverroutes now owns the driver websocket mount previously registered inline in main.go.
Legacy GET /v1/fleet/manifest is preserved as compatibility alias while mobile clients migrate to GET /v1/driver/manifest.

High-consequence driver mutations (/v1/order/deliver, /v1/order/confirm-offload, /v1/order/complete, /v1/order/collect-cash, /v1/delivery/arrive) now send deterministic Idempotency-Key headers from both Android and iOS clients for replay-safe retries.
Driver availability toggles emit DRIVER_AVAILABILITY_CHANGED inside the same Spanner ReadWriteTransaction via outbox; kafka.EmitNotification remains post-commit best-effort fanout.

Driver login/profile payloads include additive dual-node fields (home_node_type, home_node_id, driver_mode, factory metadata) so one driver app role row can operate both factory-transfer and warehouse-delivery assignments.
Factory portal shell now hydrates identity from GET /v1/factory/profile instead of static labeling.

Android and iOS clients expose additive advanced-factory endpoint methods (transfers/create, manifests detail/transition, fleet split lists, staff detail) while preserving the existing operator-loop routes.
Factory role-row realtime contract now includes GET /v1/ws/factory with additive events FACTORY_SUPPLY_REQUEST_UPDATE, FACTORY_TRANSFER_UPDATE, FACTORY_MANIFEST_UPDATE, and FACTORY_OUTBOX_FAILED.
Factory websocket envelopes include stable trace_id keys so portal and native clients can correlate refresh-triggered updates.
Portal, Android, and iOS now subscribe to websocket-triggered reloads, while polling/manual refresh remains fallback.
Route composition moved out of main.go into proximityroutes without changing the delegated proximity handlers.

Portal consumers currently depend on geo-report, dispatch-audits, zone-preview, and validate-coverage while serving-warehouse and warehouse-loads remain supplier-facing backend planning support paths.

methods: ALTER TABLE Suppliers ADD COLUMN RegionId
ALTER TABLE Warehouses ADD COLUMN RegionId
ALTER TABLE Retailers ADD COLUMN RegionId
consumers: supplier and warehouse route composers via auth.RequireRegionScopeWithClient query compatibility enforcement
future region-filtered supplier and warehouse surfaces
notes: Phase-1 rollout is additive: RegionId links remain nullable and existing country-level behavior remains default-safe.
Bootstrap seeds UZ-DEFAULT region and baseline regional config to guarantee deterministic fallback resolution.

auth/region_scope.go now provides RegionScope context injection and AppendRegionFilter helpers; supplier and warehouse role-route composers enforce region_id query compatibility for SUPPLIER/ADMIN/WAREHOUSE callers.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplierroutes while preserving the existing supplier and vault handlers.
Portal consumers currently span setup billing, profile, shift, and payment configuration as one supplier self-service contract.
Supplier gateway capability metadata now includes ADYEN manual-onboarding fields, while runtime gateway resolution is centralized in payment.NewProviderClient.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplierroutes while preserving the existing supplier handlers.
The warehouse coverage save path now updates polygon-derived H3 coverage through the same warehouse spatial outbox and cache-refresh flow as coordinate edits.

Warehouse-scoped supplier routes now inject auth.RequireWarehouseScopeWithClient(d.Spanner), constraining SupplierRole=FACTORY_ADMIN to warehouses linked through Warehouses.PrimaryFactoryId/SecondaryFactoryId; out-of-scope warehouse_id returns 403 and multi-link scope without explicit warehouse_id returns 400.
Route composition moved out of main.go into suppliercatalogroutes while preserving the existing supplier handlers and pricing services.
The supplier pricing page still relies on the existing combined GET+POST behavior of PricingService.HandleUpsertPricingRule.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplierlogisticsroutes while preserving the existing manifest service and supplier dispatch handlers.
The payload-facing manifest exception path remains inside the same extracted logistics contract to keep supplier and payload flows synchronized.
Payload terminal, payload iOS, and payload Android all depend on one payloader auth, manifest lifecycle, inbox, and websocket contract.
Shared supplier manifest routes and the payloader websocket now admit PAYLOADER alongside SUPPLIER and ADMIN on the paths the payload clients already consume.
SupplierTruckManifests remains the payload-facing manifest lifecycle source, keeping payload clients aligned on DRAFT, LOADING, SEALED, DISPATCHED, and COMPLETED states.
The payloader websocket now emits typed PAYLOAD_SYNC frames with channel SYNC so payload clients can refresh active manifest state without rendering blank notifications.

PAYLOAD_SYNC is emitted atomically on draft creation plus the supplier manifest start-loading, inject-order, seal, and manifest-exception mutation paths so other payload surfaces stay coherent after cross-device or supplier-portal changes.

Missing-items reports are additive-contract compatible for payload clients: `missing_items` remains canonical, `items` alias is accepted, and `source=PAYLOAD_TERMINAL` permits empty-item review flags.

consumers: internal ADMIN operators and diagnostics tooling
notes: Route composition moved out of main.go into simroutes while preserving handler ownership in backend-go/simulation/handler.go.
The extracted composer registers the simulation harness on chi.Router with no new DefaultServeMux mounts.
Endpoint exposure stays boot-gated by app.Simulation, which is armed only when SIMULATION_ENABLED=true.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplierinsightsroutes while preserving the existing countrycfg, analytics, and supplier handlers.

The extracted composer keeps the warehouse-scoped analytics middleware for transit, throughput, load-distribution, node-efficiency, SLA, revenue, and top-retailers via auth.RequireWarehouseScopeWithClient(d.Spanner).
Supplier CRM list/detail payloads now include additive retailer email for the admin-portal contact drawer consumer.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplieroperationsroutes while preserving the existing supplier fleet, returns, reconcile, and order handlers.
The fulfillment payment trigger keeps its prior idempotency wrapper and HTTP error mapping while moving into an extracted composer.
Route composition moved out of main.go into supplierplanningroutes while preserving the existing supplier, factory, and proximity handlers.
Cron startup for replenishment remains in main.go; the extracted composer only owns the supplier-facing HTTP planning surface.
Supplier factory create/list/detail/profile payloads now persist and return additive h3_index and product_types metadata for the admin-portal factory planning consumers.

Supply-lane mutate actions now resolve organisation supplier scope via claims.ResolveSupplierID() and honor PATCH for plain lane updates, preventing success-shaped no-ops for supplier planning consumers.
Route composition moved out of main.go into suppliercoreroutes while preserving the existing order, analytics, and supplier handlers.
After this extraction, backend-go/main.go no longer registers any /v1/supplier/* routes inline.
Supplier inventory now honors the mounted root PATCH /v1/supplier/inventory contract and returns additive sku_id/product_name aliases on inventory and audit rows for the admin-portal consumer.

ORDER_REASSIGNED now carries additive supplier_id from the reassign producer, dispatcher fanout resolves supplier recipients via payload plus order lookup fallback, and admin-portal supplier dashboard/orders/fleet views subscribe to ORDER_REASSIGNED invalidation for immediate refresh.
Inventory compatibility accepts q and search filters and accepts sku_id or product_id on mutations.
Inventory responses expose both inventory and items collections plus sku_id and product_id aliases.
Staff create accepts an optional pin and returns the effective one-time pin for native client parity.
Vehicle responses expose both max_volume_vu and capacity_vu plus a derived availability status.
Vehicle availability is schema-backed with Vehicles.UnavailableReason and travels across the warehouse portal, iOS, and Android fleet clients.
Warehouse fleet controls now share driver assign/reset and vehicle activate/deactivate mutations across portal, iOS, and Android.
Warehouse dispatch preview excludes inactive vehicles from the available-driver list so vehicle availability mutations affect dispatch eligibility immediately.
Driver list payloads now carry assigned vehicle availability metadata, and dispatch preview publishes both available_drivers and unavailable_drivers so warehouse clients can explain blocked drivers.
BroadcastSupplyRequestUpdate is defined in apps/backend-go/ws/warehouse_hub.go and called from apps/backend-go/warehouse/supply_requests.go after create and transition commits.
BroadcastDispatchLockChange is defined in apps/backend-go/ws/warehouse_hub.go and called from apps/backend-go/warehouse/dispatch_lock.go after acquire and release commits.
Portal and native warehouse clients subscribe to SUPPLY_REQUEST_UPDATE and DISPATCH_LOCK_CHANGE with warehouse-scoped filtering.
Portal, iOS, and Android clients auto-reconnect and expose reconnecting/offline live state instead of silently freezing.

Warehouse mobile dispatch surfaces create demand-forecast-backed supply requests and cancel warehouse-owned requests through apps/warehouse-app-ios/WarehouseApp/Services/WarehouseService.swift and apps/warehouse-app-android/app/src/main/java/com/pegasus/warehouse/data/remote/WarehouseApi.kt.
Warehouse portal and native clients acquire and release MANUAL_DISPATCH locks against the same dispatch-lock contract.
Dispatch control parity now spans portal, iOS, and Android warehouse clients.
dispatch_lock.go now enforces JWT-scoped lock list/release behavior for warehouse/factory callers with explicit 403 on out-of-scope lock actions.
Warehouse portal and native dispatch clients map 403 responses for lock and dispatch actions to explicit restricted-state UX feedback.
